MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

Broadly-firing "mid-clause continuation" neuron: it gives moderate-to-high activation on tokens well inside sentences of informal user-generated review/comment prose (peaking on determiners/adverbs/adjectives like "this", "that", "all", "suddenly", "fantastic", "member"), and is strongly suppressed on capitalized sentence-initial words at the very start of a document ("Do", "In").

L31·N12004unmasked layer
This neuron gives mild positive activation on ordinary-prose content words closing a clause or list item (final noun/verb like "die", "bread", "day", "designer", "exists"), while its strongest (large negative) responses are on tokens that immediately precede digits — "$", "=", or a bare space before a number in URLs, prices, and measurements.

L31·N14276unmasked layer
This neuron fires on mid-sentence tokens inside flowing, grammatical prose clauses (e.g. the subject "I", the auxiliary "be"/"have", a noun completing a compound, a closing paren before a verb) — essentially marking "a real sentence is in progress"; it is strongly suppressed on tokens in fragmentary list/heading/title text (colons in timestamps, title abbreviations like "SVP", product-name subwords, stray spaces in caption lists).
